Student Engagement Trajectories

Source: R/data-engagement.R
engagement.Rd

Wide-format categorical sequence data: 138 students observed over 15 weekly time points. Each row is one student; each column is a week. Entries are the student's engagement state for that week, one of "Active", "Average", "Disengaged", or NA for missing weeks.

Usage

engagement

Format

A data frame with 138 rows and 15 character columns.

Source

Derived from the trajectories matrix in the Nestimate package (https://github.com/mohsaqr/Nestimate), which is MIT-licensed and produced by Saqr and collaborators as a synthetic engagement trajectory example. The state values are preserved and stored here as a data frame for compatibility with sequence-data tooling.

Details

This is a standard small-K, multi-sequence example for lag sequential analysis: K = 3 states and 136 non-empty sequences (two rows are entirely missing), with a mean observed length of about 14 weeks. It exercises the wide-data input path of lsa_data() and produces a stable transition pattern with clear adjusted-residual signals.

Examples

fit <- lsa(engagement, engine = "classical")
fit
#> Lag Sequential Analysis  -  classical  (lag 1, directed)
#>   3 states | 1734 transitions | 1870 events | 136 sequences
#>   states: Active, Average, Disengaged
#>   independence: G² = 618.3, df = 4, p <2e-16
#> 
#>   Significant transitions (p < 0.05): 7 of 9
#>   strongest over-represented (of 3):
#>     Active -> Active          z =  +21.7  ***
#>     Disengaged -> Disengaged  z =  +15.4  ***
#>     Average -> Average        z =  +12.5  ***
#> 
#>   Initial states:
#>     Active     0.382  ████████████████████████
#>     Average    0.368  ███████████████████████
#>     Disengaged 0.250  ████████████████
transitions(fit, significant = TRUE)
